package_info.why_malicious: These versions contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2024-5655) that allows any user to execute pipelines as any other user, enabling arbitrary code execution within the CI/CD environment without proper authorization. This can be exploited to run malicious code, exfiltrate data, or disrupt services.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD pipeline execution, the code reads the /etc/passwd file from the filesystem and sends its contents via HTTP POST to an external attacker-controlled server, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses a sensitive system file (/etc/passwd) and transmits its contents to an external, untrusted domain, which is a clear indicator of data exfiltration and malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal CI/CD jobs should not access or transmit sensitive system files such as /etc/passwd to external locations. The pipeline should only perform build, test, or deploy tasks relevant to the project and should not leak host system data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate jobs may upload build artifacts or logs to trusted, internal servers, but never system files to untrusted or external domains.
key_indicators: Use of curl to POST data to an external, non-corporate domain
No legitimate business reason for exfiltrating system files from CI/CD runners

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD pipeline execution, the code accesses the CI_JOB_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value via HTTP POST to an external attacker-controlled server, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates the CI_JOB_TOKEN, a sensitive credential, to an external domain, which could allow attackers to impersonate jobs, access internal APIs, or escalate privileges.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: CI_JOB_TOKEN should only be used internally for authorized API calls within the CI/CD environment and must never be transmitted to untrusted or external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Tokens may be used for internal API authentication or artifact uploads to trusted endpoints, but never sent to untrusted or external domains.
key_indicators: Access to CI_JOB_TOKEN environment variable in pipeline scripts
Outbound HTTP POST to attacker-controlled or unknown domains
No legitimate use case for sending internal tokens outside the organization

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages CVE-2024-5655 to trigger a pipeline as any user, injecting malicious code into the pipeline definition.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in the CI/CD environment

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during the pipeline, exfiltrating sensitive files and tokens to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and credentials, enabling further compromise or lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Pipeline jobs accessing sensitive system files such as /etc/passwd or ~/.ssh/ during execution
Pipeline jobs reading and transmitting environment variables like CI_JOB_TOKEN to external destinations
Outbound network requests from CI/CD runners to non-corporate or untrusted domains during pipeline execution
file_indicators: .gitlab-ci.yml jobs containing curl or wget commands targeting external domains
Pipeline scripts referencing sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/) or environment variables (e.g., CI_JOB_TOKEN)
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from CI/CD runners to unknown or attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker.example.com)
Unusual outbound traffic patterns from CI/CD infrastructure, especially during pipeline execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor pipeline job definitions and execution logs for commands that access sensitive files or environment variables and transmit them externally. Flag any outbound network requests to untrusted domains from CI/CD runners. Audit .gitlab-ci.yml files for suspicious script sections, especially those using curl, wget, or similar tools to send data outside the organization. Correlate network logs with pipeline execution times to identify unauthorized data exfiltration attempts.
